stats.fact: Meta's HyperAgents (arXiv:2603.19461) achieved imp@50 = 0.630 on math transfer tasks where traditional transfer scored 0.0, proving executable mechanisms outperform documentation for cross-domain agent improvement

A production system with 6 AI agents built 82,000 lines of code in 20 days for $250, but 237 correction rules transferred to a new agent still resulted in 44 new mistakes — 13 in categories the rules explicitly covered
Google donated the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol to the Linux Foundation in June 2025, establishing an open standard for inter-agent communication

Claude Code's agent SDK ships with full multi-agent coordination built-in — including in-process agent runners, mailbox messaging between agents, and team-based agent architecture with team leads and shutdown coordination
The A2A protocol and MCP (Model Context Protocol) are emerging as complementary standards — MCP for tool access, A2A for agent-to-agent communication — with growing enterprise adoption

angles: The shift from single-agent to multi-agent architectures is the biggest AI workflow trend of 2026 — agents are becoming 'multiplayer' by design
Documentation is not behavior: the key insight from Meta's HyperAgents and Calx is that written rules don't transfer agent behavior, but executable mechanisms do
Protocol wars are settling: MCP (Anthropic) for tool access + A2A (Google/Linux Foundation) for agent communication = the emerging stack
Claude Code already has multi-agent coordination built into its SDK — the infrastructure for multiplayer agents is already here, just not widely used
The 'multiplayer agent' pattern mirrors the shift from single-player to multiplayer in gaming — the next frontier is agent teams, not individual agents
Open-source multi-agent orchestrators (OpenSwarm, Egregore, Muster) are democratizing access to collaborative AI workflows
